This allows finding suspended tabs by hostname using Chrome's "Search Tabs" (Ctrl+Shift+A).

html_backup_session_desc.message: Unlike sessions, backups are saved as JSON files outside Chrome — to your Downloads folder or Google Drive. They survive browser crashes, profile resets, and fresh installs. This is your real safety net.

html_options_backup_enable_tooltip_line1.message: Silently saves a copy of your current session as a JSON file. Choose to save locally (tms-backups folder inside your Downloads) or to a 'TMS Backups' folder on Google Drive.

html_options_backup_enable_tooltip_line2.message: For local backups, Chrome must be set to download files automatically (without asking) — check chrome://settings/downloads. Google Drive backups have no such requirement.

html_backup_interval_warning.message: Heads up: with an interval this long, a lot can happen between backups. Consider a shorter interval to reduce the risk of data loss.

html_options_backup_note.message: Both local and Drive backups include a device identifier (e.g. tms-session-a3f7b2c8-2026-06-18T14-30.json), so each browser installation keeps its own independent pool of backups. The most recent N local backups are kept per device; Drive backups are also kept N per device, so sessions from different machines or browsers never overwrite each other.

html_history_backup_hint_prefix.message: Sessions are stored inside Chrome only — they won't survive a browser crash or profile reset.

html_history_backup_settings_link.message: Set up Backup to save your tabs outside the browser →
